lines.speaker: mercutio_escalus
lines.text: Okay, can everybody see my screen? I'm getting a thumbs up from Juliet and, uh, a blank stare from Romeo.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: I can see it. That's just my face.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Yeah, we've got it. Go ahead, Mercutio.

lines.speaker: mercutio_escalus
lines.text: So this is the sync status screen for Schema Bridge, living inside Balcony. An inspector finishes a dock inspection, taps save, and this is where they find out what happened to it. Three states. Queued, sent, and needs attention.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Okay, I like that it's only three.

lines.speaker: mercutio_escalus
lines.text: Right? I had seven at one point. There was a state called 'pending, but emotionally'. I cut it.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Good call.

lines.speaker: mercutio_escalus
lines.text: Also, before anyone asks, my working name for this screen is the balcony scene.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: mercutio_escalus
lines.text: Hear me out. It's literally the Balcony App.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: No. Absolutely not. It's going in front of a freight company on Friday. It's the sync screen. Okay, walk me through queued.

lines.speaker: mercutio_escalus
lines.text: So, queued means it's saved on the device and it hasn't gone to Mesh Routing yet. Usually because they're out in a yard with no signal. Which, from what Benvolio says, is like half the day for these folks.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Romeo, is that honest? Like, if it says queued, is it actually safe?

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Yeah. That's the whole point of the local queue. The inspection gets written to the queue on the device before we try to send anything. So queued really means it's on disk and it'll go out when there's a connection. It's not a hope, it's a fact.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Okay, good. That's the thing I care about. I don't want queued to secretly mean 'probably lost'.

lines.speaker: mercutio_escalus
lines.text: Cool. So then sent is, um, it's boring on purpose. Green check, timestamp. Done. Nobody needs to think about it.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Boring is great.

lines.speaker: mercutio_escalus
lines.text: And needs attention is the one where a human has to do something. Like a sync conflict, or a photo that failed to upload. It tells you which inspection and what to tap.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: That's where Balthasar's bug would show up, right? The offline-sync conflict?

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Yeah, that's exactly the case. Two edits to the same inspection while offline.

lines.speaker: mercutio_escalus
lines.text: So, okay, here's my actual question for you two. When things are queued, I've got a little spinner up top. Like, it's working on it.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Hmm. I'm not sure about the spinner.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Yeah, I'd kill the spinner.

lines.speaker: mercutio_escalus
lines.text: Wow. Both of you. Okay, why?

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Because if they're offline, nothing is working on it. It's just waiting. A spinner sort of lies about that.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: And if I'm an inspector and I see a spinner for forty minutes, I'm going to think it's broken and, like, force quit the app. What I'd want to see is a number. Twelve inspections queued. And then it goes down when you get signal.

lines.speaker: mercutio_escalus
lines.text: Oh, that's nice. The number going down is actually satisfying. It's like a little countdown.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: And it's true. The count comes straight from the queue, so it's always accurate.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Okay, so let's decide it. We show the count of queued inspections, and we never use a spinner on this screen. Agreed?

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Agreed.

lines.speaker: mercutio_escalus
lines.text: Agreed. Rest in peace, spinner. Okay, I'll redo it with the count up top and the list underneath, grouped by state.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Can you put it on the beta board so I can track it? I'm doing triage this afternoon.

lines.speaker: mercutio_escalus
lines.text: Yep, put it under me.

lines.speaker: juliet_capulet
lines.text: Perfect. Thanks, both of you. That was fast.

lines.speaker: romeo_montague
lines.text: Thanks. I'll ping you when the queue's ready to break.
